# Style and theme

::: warning Preview version
The jsMind V2 programming API is currently a preview. The API will change in later updates. Please check this documentation anytime for the interface that is current.
:::

Visual overrides on a map, a node, or an edge. Unset fields fall back to the theme.

This page is generated from the published typings `dist/jsmind.d.ts` with TypeDoc.

## JmNodeStyle {#JmNodeStyle}

*Interface*

Visual overrides for a single node.

**Remarks**

Every field is optional and unset fields fall back to the theme. The node
carries only what differs from the theme, so a theme change still reaches
every node that did not explicitly override anything.

`incoming` lives on the child node: a line connects exactly one child, which
makes the child the natural owner. The name mirrors the layout layer
(`calculateNodeIncomingPoint` / `calculateNodeOutgoingPoint`).

**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `background` (optional) | string | Background color, e.g. `#ffffff`. |
| `borderColor` (optional) | string | Border color. |
| `borderStyle` (optional) | [JmLinePattern](/en/reference/api/style#JmLinePattern) | Border dash style. |
| `borderWidth` (optional) | number | Border width in pixels. |
| `color` (optional) | string | Text color. |
| `fontSize` (optional) | number | Font size in pixels. |
| `fontWeight` (optional) | [JmFontWeight](/en/reference/api/style#JmFontWeight) | Font weight. |
| `incoming` (optional) | [JmLineStyle](/en/reference/api/style#JmLineStyle) | Style of the line connecting this node to its parent. |
| `tone` (optional) | [JmTone](/en/reference/api/style#JmTone) | Semantic tone for this node. Overrides background/border/color from the theme. |

## JmLineStyle {#JmLineStyle}

*Interface*

Visual style of a single line.

**Remarks**

Shared by two places: `JmNodeStyle.incoming` (the line connecting a node to
its parent) and `JmEdge.style` (lines for additional, non-hierarchical
relationships). One shape avoids two vocabularies for the same thing.

**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `color` (optional) | string | Line color, e.g. `#4a9eff`. |
| `curve` (optional) | [JmLineCurve](/en/reference/api/style#JmLineCurve) | How the line travels between its endpoints. Defaults to `bezier`. |
| `pattern` (optional) | [JmLinePattern](/en/reference/api/style#JmLinePattern) | Line pattern. |
| `width` (optional) | number | Line width in pixels. |

## JmStyle {#JmStyle}

*Interface*

Style declaration for a whole mind map, as stored in the data file.

**Remarks**

Named in the singular, like the per-node and per-edge style fields: one
`style` concept, with the scope decided by where it sits. `mind.style` covers
the whole map; `node.style` covers one node; `edge.style` covers one edge.
Carrying both `styles` and `style` in one document only differed by an `s`,
which is a trap for an agent generating the JSON.

Read this as: "this mind map looks like this — it inherits from `theme`, then
overrides the fields listed below."

Splitting inheritance from overrides into one flat declaration avoids the
ambiguity of a nested `{ name, ...overrides }` form, where `name` could be
read either as "what this theme is called" or as "which theme to inherit".
Here `theme` can only mean the latter.

- `theme` names a built-in preset to inherit from. Omitted means `"default"`,
so a file that only overrides a few colors does not have to name it.
- Every other field is an override applied on top of that preset, merged
deeply.

**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `background` (optional) | string | Canvas background color. |
| `expander` (optional) | `Partial`<[JmThemeExpander](/en/reference/api/style#JmThemeExpander)> | Expander geometry overrides. |
| `line` (optional) | `Partial`<[JmThemeLine](/en/reference/api/style#JmThemeLine)> | Line geometry overrides. |
| `node` (optional) | [JmThemeNodeOverride](/en/reference/api/style#JmThemeNodeOverride) | Node geometry overrides. |
| `theme` (optional) | string | Name of the built-in theme to inherit from. Defaults to `"default"`. |
| `tones` (optional) | `Partial`<`Record`<[JmTone](/en/reference/api/style#JmTone), `Partial`<[JmTonePalette](/en/reference/api/style#JmTonePalette)>>> | Per-tone color overrides. |

## JmThemeShadow {#JmThemeShadow}

*Interface*

Drop shadows for the three visual states a node can be in.

**Remarks**

States live in the theme rather than in CSS because they change the node's
appearance, and "how does this node look" belongs with the rest of the
appearance. `normal` is the resting state; `hover` and `selected` are what
the pointer and the selection do to it.

**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hover` | [JmThemeShadowLayer](/en/reference/api/style#JmThemeShadowLayer) | Shadow while the pointer is over the node. |
| `normal` | [JmThemeShadowLayer](/en/reference/api/style#JmThemeShadowLayer) | Shadow when the node is idle. |
| `selected` | [JmThemeShadowLayer](/en/reference/api/style#JmThemeShadowLayer) | Shadow when the node is selected. |

## JmThemeShadowLayer {#JmThemeShadowLayer}

*Interface*

One drop shadow, in CSS terms.

**Remarks**

Spelled out as four numbers and a color rather than kept as a CSS string
like `"1px 1px 1px #666"` so it can be merged field by field — an override
that changes only the blur should not have to restate the offsets — and so
an agent writing the JSON never has to get CSS shorthand syntax right.

**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `blur` | number | Blur radius in pixels. |
| `color` | string | Shadow color, e.g. `#666666`. |
| `offsetX` | number | Horizontal offset in pixels. |
| `offsetY` | number | Vertical offset in pixels. |

## JmThemeShadowOverride {#JmThemeShadowOverride}

*Interface*

A partial replacement for [JmThemeShadow](/en/reference/api/style#JmThemeShadow).

**Remarks**

Every level is optional so a style can restyle one state, or one field of one
state (`hover.blur`), without restating the rest. The merged result is always
complete.

**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hover` (optional) | `Partial`<[JmThemeShadowLayer](/en/reference/api/style#JmThemeShadowLayer)> | Override for the hover shadow. |
| `normal` (optional) | `Partial`<[JmThemeShadowLayer](/en/reference/api/style#JmThemeShadowLayer)> | Override for the idle shadow. |
| `selected` (optional) | `Partial`<[JmThemeShadowLayer](/en/reference/api/style#JmThemeShadowLayer)> | Override for the selected shadow. |

## JmThemeNodeOverride {#JmThemeNodeOverride}

*Type*

Partial overrides for [JmThemeNode](/en/reference/api/style#JmThemeNode).

**Remarks**

Identical to `Partial<JmThemeNode>` except for `shadow`, which allows
overriding a single state rather than all three.

## JmTonePalette {#JmTonePalette}

*Interface*

Colors a tone resolves to.

**Remarks**

`line` is the color of the connecting line, which usually differs from
`border` so that a subtree reads as one visual grouping.

**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `borderColor` | string | Node border color. |
| `fillColor` | string | Node background color. |
| `lineColor` | string | Connecting line color. |
| `textColor` | string | Node text color. |

## JmTone {#JmTone}

*Enumeration*

Semantic tone. Expresses color only, never geometry.

**Remarks**

Semantic roles are about color; geometry is orthogonal (a node can be
warning-colored, thick-bordered and large-font at once). Keeping them apart
gives the agent fewer side effects per change, which makes generated output
more controllable.

**Members**

| Name | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Accent` | `"accent"` | Accent tone for an element that stands out without carrying a judgement. |
| `Danger` | `"danger"` | Danger or negative tone. |
| `Default` | `"default"` | Default tone, resolved from the theme's neutral palette. |
| `Info` | `"info"` | Informational or neutral-accent tone. |
| `Primary` | `"primary"` | Primary or emphasis tone. |
| `Success` | `"success"` | Success or positive tone. |
| `Warning` | `"warning"` | Warning or caution tone. |

## JmFontWeight {#JmFontWeight}

*Enumeration*

Font weight.

**Remarks**

An enum rather than an inline union so the CLI can enumerate the accepted
values instead of repeating them. `JmLinePattern` and `JmLineCurve` had this
shape already; `fontWeight` was the odd one out.

**Members**

| Name | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Bold` | `"bold"` | Emphasised weight. |
| `Normal` | `"normal"` | Regular weight. |

## JmLinePattern {#JmLinePattern}

*Enumeration*

Line dash style.

**Members**

| Name | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Dashed` | `"dashed"` | Dashed line. |
| `Dotted` | `"dotted"` | Dotted line. |
| `Solid` | `"solid"` | Continuous line. |

## JmLineCurve {#JmLineCurve}

*Enumeration*

How a line travels between its two endpoints.

**Remarks**

A different axis from [JmLinePattern](/en/reference/api/style#JmLinePattern): `pattern` says whether the
stroke is dashed, `curve` says what shape it traces. They are separable on
purpose - a straight dashed line and a curved dashed line both need to exist,
and a single `style` string (as in v1's `line_style`) could only ever express
one of the two.

**Members**

| Name | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Bezier` | `"bezier"` | Cubic bezier leaving each endpoint horizontally. |
| `Straight` | `"straight"` | Straight segment from one endpoint to the other. |
